question: What is the primary purpose of evaluation in nursing education?

options.A: Determining if students meet learning objectives
options.B: Punishing students who fail clinical rotations

explanation: Evaluation systematically checks whether students are successfully achieving established academic and clinical goals. [learn more](GST321_U9_T3#GST321_U9_T3_h1)

question: Why must nurse educators use multiple assessment methods instead of just one?

options.A: Single tests take too long to grade properly
options.B: School accreditation boards demand at least ten test types
options.C: Nursing requires theory, practical skills, and professional values
options.D: Students get bored taking the same type of exam

explanation: A single testing format cannot capture the diverse competencies required for safe nursing practice. [learn more](GST321_U9_T3#GST321_U9_T3_h1)

question: A quiz given at the end of a semester to assign a final grade is an example of what?
explanation: Summative evaluations happen at the end of learning periods to measure overall achievement and assign final grades. [learn more](GST321_U9_T3#GST321_U9_T3_h2)

question: What is the main benefit of formative feedback during clinical ward practice?

options.A: Determining who passes or fails the entire school
options.B: Helping students correct errors before final grading
options.C: Ranking students against each other in clinical groups
options.D: Providing permanent records for the nursing council

explanation: Formative assessment guides learners while they are still developing skills, allowing them to fix mistakes early. [learn more](GST321_U9_T3#GST321_U9_T3_h2)

question: What learning domain do written examinations primarily measure?
explanation: Written tests focus on mental skills, knowledge retention, and intellectual reasoning. [learn more](GST321_U9_T3#GST321_U9_T3_h3)

question: Why should nursing multiple-choice questions use patient scenarios instead of simple definitions?

options.A: To confuse students who studied too fast
options.B: To test spelling rather than medical facts
options.C: To test clinical reasoning and application
options.D: To make the exam paper look longer and harder

explanation: Scenario-based questions evaluate a student's ability to think critically and apply knowledge to real patient situations. [learn more](GST321_U9_T3#GST321_U9_T3_h3)

question: An intravenous cannulation procedure performed by a student is evaluated under which learning domain?
explanation: Hands-on physical procedures and motor skills fall under the psychomotor domain. [learn more](GST321_U9_T3#GST321_U9_T3_h4)

question: What is the primary advantage of using simulation laboratories for psychomotor assessment?

options.A: Students feel zero stress during simulated exams
options.B: Educators do not need to watch the students work
options.C: Students can practice high-risk tasks without harming patients
options.D: Simulation equipment never breaks down like hospital gear

explanation: Simulation provides a safe space for learners to build manual dexterity and confidence before touching real patients. [learn more](GST321_U9_T3#GST321_U9_T3_h4)

question: Which student trait is best evaluated through the affective domain?
explanation: The affective domain covers attitudes, values, and professional behaviors like empathy and ethics. [learn more](GST321_U9_T3#GST321_U9_T3_h5)

question: Why is assessing the affective domain challenging for nursing educators?

options.A: There are no written guidelines for professional behavior
options.B: Patients always interfere with teacher evaluations
options.C: It relies heavily on subjective observation and personal bias
options.D: Students refuse to show their true feelings on the ward

explanation: Measuring attitudes and values involves subjective judgment, requiring educators to rely on clear behavioral anchors to remain fair. [learn more](GST321_U9_T3#GST321_U9_T3_h5)

question: A clinical tool that simply marks steps as either done or not done is called what?
explanation: Checklists use a yes/no or present/absent format to confirm the completion of specific action steps. [learn more](GST321_U9_T3#GST321_U9_T3_h6)

question: When should an educator choose a rating scale over a simple checklist?

options.A: When students are taking a written theory exam
options.B: When the quality and independence of the performance matter
options.C: When the instructor has no time to watch the student
options.D: When there is only one correct way to do a procedure

explanation: Rating scales allow educators to grade nuances in performance quality, such as smoothness and patient communication. [learn more](GST321_U9_T3#GST321_U9_T3_h6)

question: What is the primary goal of student self-assessment in nursing clinicals?

options.A: Replacing the final grade given by the instructor
options.C: Allowing students to choose their own clinical hours
options.D: Reducing the workload of the clinical preceptor

explanation: Self-assessment helps students recognize their own strengths and areas needing improvement. [learn more](GST321_U9_T3#GST321_U9_T3_h7)

question: Why might students struggle with giving accurate peer evaluations during group work?

options.A: Fear of damaging personal friendships with classmates
options.B: Lack of access to official school computers
options.C: Strict hospital policies against student talking

explanation: Peer evaluation can create social discomfort, leading students to give overly lenient scores to friends. [learn more](GST321_U9_T3#GST321_U9_T3_h7)

question: What term describes an assessment tool that consistently measures what it is supposed to measure?
explanation: Validity ensures that a test or tool accurately measures the specific learning objective it was designed for. [learn more](GST321_U9_T3#GST321_U9_T3_h8)

question: How can nursing faculty improve the reliability of clinical grading among different instructors?

options.A: Using standardized grading rubrics and preceptor training
options.B: Giving every student the exact same final grade
options.C: Eliminating all practical exams from the curriculum
options.D: Allowing every clinical instructor to make up their own rules

explanation: Clear rubrics and aligned training ensure different educators interpret student performance consistently. [learn more](GST321_U9_T3#GST321_U9_T3_h8)
